# Quagga2 scanner distribution

`public/quagga-1.13.0.min.js` consists of a notice header followed by the unchanged `dist/quagga.min.js` from npm `@ericblade/quagga2` 1.13.0 (MIT), tarball SHA-256 `bcd9f3f4df8d735fec260a0d7c7a1bb5a04ee7ec568fa240bc9b045988542da7`; original minified distribution SHA-256 `dec8edc93a6b394f091d2415da26f1e9535bbc5df4893bdb8e673e707b095f99`. Loading is same-origin and begins only after an explicit scanner request. The application captures frames from its own camera stream and uses Quagga's documented `decodeSingle` API with `numOfWorkers: 0`; it does not modify decoder internals or use Quagga's global camera singleton.

The unminified distribution's embedded source map contains 248 sources: 148 lodash modules, 40 @babel/runtime modules, 5 gl-matrix modules, Quagga source and webpack infrastructure. All source-map dependency contents byte-match npm lodash 4.18.1, @babel/runtime 7.28.4 and gl-matrix 3.4.4 respectively; matching content is not proof of the packager's exact dependency lock. Source-content notice scan found the regenerator-runtime Facebook copyright and MIT license notice and no GPL/Oracle header. The served file retains that notice and complete MIT license texts for Quagga, gl-matrix, lodash and Babel, also stored beside this file. This inventory does not constitute legal advice.

To reproduce the served asset, extract the pinned Quagga tarball, then run `node vendor/quagga-1.13.0/prepend-notices.cjs path/to/dist/quagga.min.js public/quagga-1.13.0.min.js`; verify the input digest and the output hash in the task receipt. No package download occurs during the normal app build.
